display.title: Haggadah in Yiddish: The Title Page and the Leaping Deer
display.summary_short: A short Yiddish introduction for children to the Haggadah's title page, with its picture of a deer leaping over the mountains.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish to children, this short introduction opens the Haggadah at its first page. The title page shows a deer leaping over the mountains, with the words from Shir HaShirim, 'leaping over the mountains; my Beloved is like a deer'. The teacher explains that the verse speaks of the redemption from Egypt and of the redemption through Moshiach. At the plague of the firstborn Hashem 'leaped' over the Jewish houses, and that is why the festival is called Pesach, which means passing or leaping over. Just as a deer leaps quickly over the mountains, so Moshiach will come quickly, leaping over the times, and bring us straight into the Geulah.
display.lesson: Just as Hashem passed over the Jewish houses in Egypt, Moshiach will come swiftly, like a deer leaping over mountains.

segments.title: The Haggadah's title page
segments.summary: The leaping deer, the name Pesach, and Moshiach who will come quickly.
